sam_w: Quick idea — can we split the "golden signal" onboarding gate into two distinct signals: soundness (quality/regressions) and compatibility/surface checks? The current monolithic gate is making onboarding take forever for models that are fine but fail a heavy bench step.

kira: +1 to the split concept. Example: yesterday a quantized Llama variant failed because the tokenizer normalization differs; it passes generation smoke but blows up in deep eval.

sam_w: Exactly. My thought: enforce a lightweight fast_smoke gate that runs in ~5m for format/compat (tokenizer, init, small forward pass, KV shape) and defer deep bench (throughput, tail latency, quality evals) to an asynchronous deep_bench that can run up to a few hours. If deep_bench fails we mark model as "quarantine" but keep it available behind a canary flag.

devin_r: Love it. Operationally we need concrete acceptance criteria for both. Proposal sketch: 
```
gates:
  fast_smoke:
    timeout: 5m
    checks: [tokenize, init_forward, kv_shape, simple_inference]
    pass_criteria: all_checks_pass

  deep_bench:
    timeout: 2h
    checks: [throughput, p95_latency, quality_regressions, memory_leak]
    pass_criteria: p95 < threshold AND quality delta <= 0.02
```
This keeps the runtime path short for most onboarding flows.

lia_m: Two operational questions: 1) What's the rollback/availability behavior if deep_bench fails after fast_smoke passed and we've already started routing canary traffic? 2) How does this interact with Dedicated reserved pools and quota enforcement?

sam_w: For 1) my thinking: canary traffic = very small traffic tag; if deep_bench fails we auto-swap routing to a fallback compatible model and add the failed model to a quarantine bucket for fixes. For 2) dedicated pools should be able to opt into immediate deep_bench scheduling (if they bought the runway), otherwise deep_bench runs on shared infra with backpressure. We'll need an explicit policy flag on model metadata: `deep_bench_priority: dedicated|deferred`.

bench-bot: Summary: recent onboarding runs — median fast_smoke time = 3m12s, median deep_bench time = 1h42m; ~18% of models fail deep_bench but pass fast_smoke (most common failures: quality_regressions, tokenizer edgecases). See /bench/runs/last-7d

kira: If we quarantine rather than block, we reduce churn for PR-based model additions. But we should add a clear triage workflow: auto-attach the failing artifacts (sample diffs, tokenizer dump, failing inputs) so ML engineers can triage quickly.

devin_r: Agree. Also want a minimal contract for the fast_smoke check set so infra teams can implement a fast path in runtime. Things to include: deterministic tokenization check, forward-pass shape + small seqlen perf, kv cache roundtrip. Keep it under ~100ms p95 per sample ideally.

sam_w: Next steps I suggest: (a) brief RFC addendum with the split proposal + config draft, (b) a short pilot to gate 10% of new models through the split flow for 2 weeks, (c) add quarantine UI in Console and a CI webhook for triage. Can folks ack and I’ll spin up the addendum? @kira @devin_r @lia_m :thumbsup:

lia_m: :thumbsup: on pilot. Need to loop in product so the Console UX is scoped.

kira: ack — will draft triage artifact contract.

devin_r: ack — I’ll proto the fast_smoke contract and run a small sweep to validate thresholds.

sam_w: sweet. I’ll write the RFC addendum and include the `deep_bench_priority` flag and the quarantine lifecycle. Planning to land the addendum by EOW, pilot next week.

bench-bot: Noted. Scheduling telemetry to surface quarantine counts in Console.
